Genesis 40 · Do Not Interpretations Belong to God
2B.21 Doubtfulness in the ways and power of God is forbidden.

precepts.text: On Herod's birthday the dancing pleased him, and the head of John the Baptist was demanded in a charger; another wicked occurrence on a birthday.
precepts.point: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

note.label: Genesis 40: Do Not Interpretations Belong to God

precepts.why:
“But when Herod’s birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.” He promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask, and she, instructed of her mother, said, “Give me here John Baptist’s head in a charger.” John the Baptist was beheaded on a birthday.

Birthdays are heathen customs, and wicked things take place at them. On Pharaoh’s birthday he made a feast unto all his servants and “hanged the chief baker”, a man put to death before everybody. On Herod’s birthday the dancing pleased him and the head of John the Baptist was demanded in a charger. Two birthdays in the scriptures, and a man dies at each one.

precepts.text: Peter walked on the water, but as soon as doubt came he began to sink; had the priests doubted and thought the water was about to fall, they could not have stood, but their feet stood firm.
precepts.point: The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order: come ye up out of Jordan. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith; they held their place in the midst of a stopped river without wavering.
precepts.why:
The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order, “Come ye up out of Jordan.” Compare Peter. “And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.” Christ caught him and said, “O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?”

Peter walked on the water, but as soon as doubt came he began to sink. Had the priests doubted and thought the water was about to fall, they could not have stood; but their feet stood firm in the midst of a stopped river without wavering. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith. And everything held its place exactly as long as Israel needed it to: only when the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land did the waters of Jordan return unto their place and flow over all his banks as before.
